properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 10:46AM CDT until July 25 at 1:45PM CDT by NWS Nashville TN
properties.description:
FFWOHX

The National Weather Service in Nashville has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Lawrence County in middle Tennessee...
Northeastern Wayne County in middle Tennessee...

* Until 145 PM CDT.

* At 1046 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lawrenceburg, Ethridge and Henryville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Cache Valley/Utah Portion
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 25 at 9:31AM MDT until July 28 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...High temperatures of up to 100 degrees, with low
temperatures in the lower to mid 70s providing little relief
overnight. HeatRisk will be in the red (major) range through the
weekend.

* WHERE...Cache Valley/Utah Portion.

* WHEN...Until midnight MDT Monday Night.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

If you do not have air conditioning in your home or lack shelter,
you can call 211 or visit 211utah.org for assistance locating
appropriate shelter from the heat.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued July 25 at 11:16AM EDT until July 26 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Gulf County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Westerly swell over the Gulf waters this
morning will combine with westerly breezes and the afternoon
seabreeze to bring development of a high risk for rip currents
this afternoon and evening, mainly over west-facing beaches of
Gulf and Bay Counties.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 25 at 9:14AM MDT until July 26 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 105 expected.

* WHERE...Cheyenne CO, Kit Carson, and Yuma Counties.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 9 PM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Saturday night and into Sunday morning are
forecast to see warm low temperatures in the upper 60s to low 70s
which could further exacerbate any heat related impacts for the day
Sunday.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Bladen, NC; Columbus, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 11:12AM EDT until July 25 at 2:15PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
FFWILM

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Bladen County in southeastern North Carolina...
Northern Columbus County in southeastern North Carolina...

* Until 215 PM EDT.

* At 1112 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated numerous showers and
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Whiteville, Chadbourn, Lake Waccamaw, Sandyfield, Hallsboro,
Emerson, Elkton, Redbug, Council, Southeastern Community College,
Carvers, Kelly, Evergreen, Bolton, East Arcadia, and Cerro Gordo.
properties.instruction:
Flash flooding from heavy rainfall can be expected, especially near
poor drainage areas and other flood prone locations. Roads may be
damaged or washed away. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles. If
flooding is observed, then turn around, don't drown.

properties.areaDesc: Brunswick, NC; New Hanover, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 25 at 11:06AM EDT until July 25 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Brunswick County in southeastern North Carolina...
New Hanover County in southeastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1104 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to showers
and thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen in some areas this morning.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wilmington, Leland, Oak Island, Carolina Beach, Wrightsville
Beach, Kure Beach, Holden Beach, Caswell Beach, Bald Head Island,
Snows Cut, South Masonboro Island, North Masonboro Island, Ocean
Crest Pier, Johnny Mercer Pier, Figure Eight Island, Boiling
Spring Lakes, St. James, Southport and Mill Creek.
- weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 1.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Tuesday morning and continue rising to 40.4 feet Thursday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 40.6
feet on 07/11/2007.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until late tomorrow morning.

* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding reaches into low
lying areas of the flood plain. Livestock should be moved from
vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 23.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 7:30 AM CDT Saturday was 25.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
late this evening and continue falling to 9.7 feet Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
23.5 feet on 07/27/1992.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight by 230 AM CDT.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON TODAY TO MIDNIGHT MDT
TONIGHT DUE TO DRY LIGHTNING FOR NORTHERN BLACK HILLS, CENTRAL BLACK
HILLS, SOUTHERN BLACK HILLS, FALL RIVER COUNTY AREA, NORTHERN FOOT
HILLS, EASTERN FOOT HILLS, CUSTER COUNTY PLAINS, PINE RIDGE AREA,
BUTTE COUNTY AREA, PERKINS COUNTY, WEST CENTRAL PLAINS, ZIEBACH
COUNTY, HAAKON COUNTY AREA, BADLANDS AREA, BENNETT COUNTY AREA,
NORTHERN CAMPBELL, SOUTHERN CAMPBELL, CROOK COUNTY PLAINS, WESTON
COUNTY PLAINS, AND WYOMING BLACK HILLS...

.Thunderstorms expected to develop across northeastern Wyoming into
western South Dakota Saturday afternoon and evening. These storms are
expected to be high based and produce frequent lightning with little
to no rainfall as they move through. The dry storm risk combined with
very hot temperatures in the upper 90s to 100s, very low humidities
of 15 to 20 percent, and dry fuels, critical fire weather conditions
are expected tomorrow afternoon and evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 319,
320, 321, 322, 323, 324, 325, 326, 327, 328, 329, 330, 331, 332,
and 333.

* TIMING...From noon today to midnight MDT tonight.

* LIGHTNING...Frequent dry lightning is possible with thunderstorms.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty and erratic winds are possible in and near
any thunderstorms.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Thunderstorms with little to no rain, gusty and
erratic winds, and frequent lightning are possible.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
expected. A combination of gusty winds, low relative humidity, and
dry lightning can contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected. Afternoon temperatures

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and

extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM TO 9 PM MDT TODAY FOR
SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FOR IDAHO FIRE WEATHER ZONES 410, 413, AND
427...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 410 Upper Snake River
Valley/Idaho Falls BLM, Fire Weather Zone 413 Caribou
Range/Caribou NF and Fire Weather Zone 427 Goose Creek and
Raft River Valley/Southern Sawtooth NF/Twin Falls BLM south of
the Snake River.

* IMPACTS...Scattered thunderstorms can produce frequent
lightning that may in turn produce wildfire starts in
receptive fuels.

* THUNDERSTORMS...A mix of wet and dry storms.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts over 35 mph with peak gusts nearing 45-
55 mph.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly based on these criteria
for Southeastern Idaho:

- Relative humidity at or below 15 percent and wind gusts of at
least 25 mph in the mountains, or 30 mph in the Snake Plain.

- Thunderstorm coverage of 25 percent, without specific rainfall
criteria.

- Other high impact events deemed critical by the National
Weather Service and area fire management agencies.

properties.areaDesc: Indian Wells Valley; Mojave Desert
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 25 at 4:47AM PDT until July 27 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures between
108 to 112 degrees and low temperatures between 75 to 83 degrees.

* WHERE...Indian Wells Valley and Mojave Desert.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 PM PDT MONDAY

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT this morning through this evening.

hypothermia to anyone immersed in the waters. Anyone on boats

number of boats and paddlecraft are expected to be out on the
water and when warm air temperatures may cause people to
underestimate the danger of the cold water. Paddle smart from the
start. Always wear your life jacket. Be aware of wind conditions,
tides, and localized currents.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat

properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.areaDesc: Grand Canyon Country
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 25 at 12:47AM MST until July 26 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures around 105 degrees at Havasupai Gardens, and
112 to 114 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 25 at 12:47AM PDT until July 25 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
...Critical fire weather conditions continue through the
weekend...

.Hot, dry and windy conditions will peak this afternoon and
Saturday east of the Cascades and potions of northern California.
Humidities nudge higher on Sunday, although winds and low rhs may
still meet red flag criteria.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire weather zone 624 covering the
Klamath Basin and Fremont-Winema National Forest. In
California, fire weather zone 285 covering Modoc County
except for Surprise Valley. The areas of concern shrink
southern portions of fwz 624 Sunday.

* WINDS...Southwest to west 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 45
mph Friday and Saturday and 35 mph Sunday.

* MINIMUM HUMIDITY...5 to 15 percent. Humidities rise slightly
onSunday.

* DURATION...3 to 8 hours Friday, Saturday and Sunday afternoon
and evening.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The fire weather threat will decrease
overnight with increasing humidities and lighter winds.
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The South Central Mountains, including the Ruidoso area
burn scars.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms will be capable of producing rainfall
rates in excess of 1 inch per hour on Ruidoso area burn scars
Saturday afternoon. This activity will move slowly and
erratically across the area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 24 at 4:19PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Idaho Department of Environmental Quality in Lewiston
Nez Perce Tribe

...AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY FOR Clearwater, Idaho, Latah, Lewis, and Nez Perce
Counties...

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...Clearwater, Idaho, Latah, Lewis, and Nez Perce Counties...

* WHEN...Until noon July 27th.

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is less likely to be affected.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Lewiston Regional Office at (208) 799-4370
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Ottawa, KS
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 24 at 6:24PM CDT until July 26 at 5:54PM CDT by NWS Topeka KS
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...

Salt Creek near Ada affecting Ottawa County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Salt Creek near Ada.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Minor low land flooding along the Salt
Creek. At 20.0 feet, 50th Road just south of the bridge over the
Salt Creek floods. At 20.2 feet, Deck of 50th Road bridge over the
Salt Creek floods. At 21.0 feet, Flood waters are over one half
mile wide over cultivated farm land 3 miles east southeast of the
town of Ada.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:45 PM CDT Friday the stage was 19.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.4 feet
tomorrow evening. It will then fall below flood stage early
Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This product along with additional weather and stream information is
available at www.weather.gov/top/.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL SUNDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 24 at 3:15PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A cold front is expected to move southeast from the Chukchi Sea
Saturday night into Sunday, northwesterly winds are expected to
increase across the Kotzebue Sound. Gusts on Sunday are expected
to be between 30 and 40 mph. With this, water levels could rise to
as high as 2 ft above the normal high tide line, with the highest
levels in the Kotzebue Sound.

NWSheadline: Slight Water Level Rises Expected Sunday

properties.areaDesc: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Arctic Plains; Central Brooks Range; Romanzof Mountains
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 24 at 3:15PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Another Arctic cold front is expected to move southeast from the
Chukchi Sea Saturday night into Sunday. Starting off, most of the
precipitation will be rain and then transition to snow Saturday
night into early Sunday morning. During this transition, there is
a slight chance for sleet and/or freezing drizzle to fall along
the eastern Arctic Coast. 2-4" of snow is possible in the Brooks
Range and a coating to 2" across the Arctic Coast.

NWSheadline: Wintry Mix Possible Across North Slope with Progressing Cold Front Saturday Night into Sunday

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 24 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Friday July 24 to 400 PM Saturday July 25

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather will allow ozone to
reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category on Friday and
Saturday. The highest concentrations are expected in the Denver
Metro Area.  For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and
advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Saturday, July 25, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:

smoke.

* WHERE...Baker County.

* WHEN...UNTIL 11 AM PDT MONDAY.

medical conditions. People most at risk to adverse health effects
include infants, young children, people with heart or lung
disease, older adults, and pregnant women.

weather. Check current conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information
Blog, DEQ's Air Quality Index, or by downloading the free
OregonAIR app on your smartphone.

ventilation systems or portable air purifiers.

levels.

healthcare provider's advice.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Saturday.

Water could enter a few low-lying cabins along the Yentna River,
particularly near Lake Creek.

- At 139 PM AKDT, recent heavy rains have caused rapid river
rises. Minor flooding is expected to continue, especially
along the Yentna River near Lake Creek.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 1:30pm the stage was 21.5 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.

At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.

At 22.0 feet: Several lodges and resorts will have water in a
number of cabins with water also encroaching the main lodge
buildings.

prepared to take action.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 22 at 5:20PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the South Coast Air Basin and Coachella Valley. Levels
of ozone pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...until 8 PM Monday. The highest ozone levels typically occur
in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT FOR HARMFUL LEVELS OF OZONE (SMOG) AIR POLLUTION
